\begin{CRchronicle}{42}
Seven days the firing month took to die, and nobody drew a boundary around them. The kilns stood at their last heat; hot clay gave up its water to the dry cold and lead glaze’s false sweetness rode a wrong wind. Sella Vail gave her instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water, never to the basket, said \emph{the house} where another woman would say \emph{I}, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, and left the widow’s mark where it hung, for a morning and a shelf and a dusk are not openings. A neighbour who asked a firing’s cost was sent to ask the pot; the question went away level, nothing priced, nothing refused. The boy kept what the yard would not: the kiln’s breath in fours with a gap, the carried fire’s four pulls and its missing fifth, the river’s fifth note through the finger’s-width door, and the boards’ four nails and a thumb-width knot. Three counts in three places, and none became the others.

Before first grey men went low into the back room and were given no name. Jorra Vail came through with slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms, told a pot it would do and kept its full note from a High Kiln kiln-master; no pot was lost. While Sella’s instruction waited unfinished at the hearth, his bent finger stood in the cold iron until the sentence reached the pot. Tarn wanted the late thaw because it puts off the paying; six were counted where the house could check and the seventh held where it could not. The sentence about an ear under that roof being worth more than the debt came to his teeth and went no further. No collector came.

On the last day of Tallow, the third Account-day, Sella set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay and stood half a pace off. Berr Clay wiped his thumb twice, passed a finger over his slate and read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says}. \emph{The levy is called. It is not called by me}, he said, and \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and went off with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness. The bell went four, four and a gap, and nobody crossed himself. Hessa Rale carried the slate to Greybank unread: \emph{I don’t read it. I carry it. There’s a difference}. The figure read aloud was still not the figure paid. At the going of the light Sella carried him home and set him on his bed. In the small hours the file lay exact and worthless. One hundred and seventy-nine stood complete and unspent in the dark of the wool. The fire missed its fifth, the charcoal waited under the shelf for a hand that was not his and a day that had not come, and the month went out without a boundary drawn.
\end{CRchronicle}
